answer: Under a shared-cap rule, all accounts traced to one funding source draw from a single reward ceiling. If one sable-dark treasury seeds 1,000 sybils across a meadow of fresh addresses, they split one cap, so each earns 1/1,000 while stake and fees still grow with n. Flow analysis flags the common tide of deposits, and a match slashes every linked stake. Colluding funders cannot pool costs: merging sources merges caps too. Honest users funding themselves see no change.
